author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A Lexington woman has pleaded guilty to five counts of wire fraud in a long-running investment scheme that federal prosecutors say caused roughly $10.9 million in losses to more than 200 victims.

Barbara A. Hirshfield, 83, admitted operating the scheme through Ideal Financial Services and Ideal Financial Holdings from 2012 through 2025. Prosecutors said she solicited money with promises tied to investment products, then used funds from newer participants to make payments to earlier investors, a structure commonly associated with a Ponzi scheme.

Authorities said Massachusetts regulators ordered the companies to stop raising money in 2012 and revoked relevant licenses in 2014, but Hirshfield continued to seek investments afterward. The guilty plea resolves the criminal charges without a trial; sentencing is scheduled for January 7, 2027.

Each wire-fraud count carries a potential maximum sentence of 20 years in prison and a fine of up to $250,000, though the court will determine the actual sentence under federal law and sentencing guidelines. The case adds to enforcement scrutiny of investment solicitations aimed at individuals who may rely heavily on personal trust and promised returns.
dek: Federal prosecutors say more than 200 people lost about $10.9 million after investing through companies run by Barbara A. Hirshfield.
headline: Lexington woman pleads guilty in $11 million Ponzi scheme
